title: A Bank and Tech Barbell
summary: Fiscal persistence, corporate Bitcoin leverage and a stock barbell.
assessment: The fiscal legislation call and AMD-over-TSM preference worked. The short-term equity ceiling and explicit six-month Bitcoin forecast failed. The leverage discussion identifies a real risk channel, but its crypto history contains chronology errors and overstates the permanence of GBTC supply removal.

claims.reason: The absence of a 2022-2023 recession supports criticism of an unadjusted leading-index signal. It does not establish fiscal dominance as the sole reason for model failure; post-pandemic sector normalization and labor conditions also matter. GDPNow is a conditional nowcast rather than a guaranteed outcome.

claims.reason: Financing-funded purchases can add demand, while debt service or refinancing stress can prompt sales. The scale of actual forced selling and its causal price impact are not established here. framework_lessons: A successful breakout does not rescue a failed six-month forecast.
A financing structure can change, so historical lockups should not be called permanent.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
